prompt: Style: a hand-made picture-book illustration, inked and painted. Line art in dark umber and deep forest-green ink, never pure black: the lines vary in weight, taper at their ends and sometimes break off or stop short of closing a shape. Colors are opaque gouache with visible dry-brush strokes and the grain of watercolor paper showing through. The characters are inked carefully; the background is painted looser, with fewer lines, soft brush edges and simple masses. Wood grain, knit and cloth are suggested with a few confident strokes, not rendered everywhere. Muted, earthy palette: rust, ochre, moss green, slate blue and warm brown, with cool blue-gray shadows. The scene: a tiny camp on the forest floor at night in steady rain, seen from a mouse's height: a huge burdock leaf bent over on its stem makes a roof over a dry patch of moss, where four small friends wait for a pot of soup to cook over a tiny fire; nothing else is there, no buildings and no camp clutter. Foreground: a sparse fringe of moss and a few broad, flat pebbles along the bottom edge, where the dry patch ends. Midground: under the leaf roof, left of center: the tiny campfire in a ring of pebbles with a little soup pot hanging over it from a tripod of three twigs; the mothling sits on the left of the fire holding its lantern, the short-horned lizard lies on the moss in front of the fire, the garter snake sits coiled on the far side of the fire; at the right edge of the leaf roof the red-backed salamander stands half in the rain holding its salal leaf over its head; clear, empty space above the pot. Background: beyond the leaf roof on the right, the open forest floor at night: dark and wet, with shallow puddles, grass stems and fern fronds rising like tall trees, and a few pale mushrooms far back. No moon and no stars. The falling rain itself is not drawn (it is animated later): the air is clear and the ground is wet. The characters, drawn exactly as described: (1) a polyphemus mothling: a round tan puff of fluff about the size of a teacup, with a fluffy collar, two whole feathery antennae, wings with big round blue-and-yellow eyespots, two tiny black dot eyes without shine, holding a short twig in one small hand, with a tiny glowing paper lantern hanging from the twig's tip on a short string, as if it brought its own light. (2) a pygmy short-horned lizard: a round, flat, sandy-gray lizard with tiny soft horns around its head, little moss tufts and a sprig of silver sagebrush growing between its spikes, two tiny black dot eyes without shine, holding nothing. (3) a northwestern garter snake: a soft, plump brown snake with an orange stripe along its back, a small fern sprout growing on its head, two tiny black dot eyes without shine, and a knitted scarf wrapped once around its neck with both ends hanging down in front. (4) a western red-backed salamander: slender, with dark gray sides speckled with white and one brick-red stripe running down its back from its head to the tip of its tail, two tiny black dot eyes without shine, standing on its hind legs and holding a big glossy salal leaf over its head like an umbrella by the leaf's stem in one hand, the leaf tilted back so its whole head and face show; nothing on its head. the fire is the main light: a small warm circle on the moss, the four friends' fronts and the underside of the burdock leaf, fading to deep green-black within a short distance. The mothling's lantern adds one smaller warm pool beside it. The salamander at the roof's edge is lit only on the side toward the fire. Most of the forest stays in cool, dark blue-green; about two thirds of the frame is dark. the camera sits low on the moss at the friends' eye level, looking slightly across the camp toward the open forest on the right. The bent burdock stem and its broad leaf frame the upper left and roof the camp. The group sits left of center; the salamander stands at the right edge of the roof; the right third is quiet, dark, wet forest floor. Locked-off, wide 16:9. Locked-off camera at eye level, wide 16:9 composition with a clear foreground, midground and background. Leave open, uncluttered areas around the light sources, the windows and the characters so they can be animated. No people anywhere: no pedestrians or silhouettes outside, no portraits, posters or statues of people. No other creatures besides the characters described: no birds, insects or snails anywhere (small creatures are animated in afterwards). No lightning bolts. Things that move are animated afterwards, so do not paint them frozen: no visible steam or smoke plumes, no water drops hanging from edges and no streams of dripping water; surfaces may look wet. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark, no user interface. It must look like a real illustrator spent days on it, with deliberate choices everywhere. Avoid every look of generic AI art: no glossy or plastic surfaces, no sparkles or glitter, no bokeh, no lens flare, no bloom halos, no glowing particles or dust motes, no god rays, no wet reflections full of glints, no sunset gradient sky, no teal-and-orange grading, no HDR rendering of every surface, no smooth airbrushed gradients, no uniform machine-clean outlines, no big shiny anime eyes, no blush stickers. Leave large areas simple and quiet; put the detail only where the eye should go.
